title: The AI Security family: AI Access Security, AI Guard (AI Guardrails), AI Red Teaming and the AI asset inventory
aliases: difference between ai guard and ai guardrails
ai security in the zscaler stack
sensitive data going into llm prompts

prose.text: Zscaler groups its AI products into one family. This subject says which part of the family answers which question before an answer goes deep.

prose.label: AI Access Security.
prose.text: {{access-security-capabilities}} The policy mechanics behind it are ZIA's: AI and ML rules in Cloud App Control, [[zia.cloud-app-control.ai-ml-rules]], prompt DLP in [[zia.dlp]], AI URL categories in [[zia.url-filtering]], decryption in [[zia.ssl-inspection]], and isolation in [[zbi.policy]].

prose.label: AI Guard and AI Guardrails.
prose.text: {{guardrails-page-is-ai-guard}} The guardrail list an earlier capture of that page gave is unverified {{gap:guardrails-page-list}}. {{guardrails-no-separate-surface}} AI Guard is in [[ai-security.ai-guard]].

prose.label: APIs.
prose.text: {{api-families}} The OneAPI base paths are in [[shared.oneapi.base-urls:base-path-table]]. The AI Infrastructure inventory and its paging rules are in [[ai-security.asset-inventory-api]]; AI Guard has its own API, in [[ai-security.ai-guard.admin-api]] and [[ai-security.ai-guard.runtime-api]].

prose.label: AI Red Teaming.
prose.text: {{red-teaming-api}} What the captures do not settle about it is open {{gap:red-teaming-boundary}}.

prose.label: Not captured.
prose.text: Packaging, licensing and per-call accounting are open {{gap:packaging}}. Hooks into other products are mapped in [[shared.integrations]].

checks.do: Which part of the family the question is about: users' access to public AI apps (ZIA Cloud App Control, DLP, URL Filtering), runtime guardrails on prompts and responses (AI Guard), testing of an organization's own AI apps (AI Red Teaming), or the AI asset and issue inventory (AI Infrastructure API).
Whether the tenant is entitled to the product before treating a page or an API operation as available; no capture settles entitlement.

four-capabilities.statement: Zscaler's AI Security product page names four areas: AI Asset Management (auto-discovering AI assets, including models, agents, MCP servers and shadow AI, and tracing data-to-AI lineage across 2,900+ apps); Secure Access to AI (blocking access by role in real time, filtering sensitive data from LLMs, governing agent-to-agent traffic); Secure AI Apps and Infrastructure (testing 5,000+ attack scenarios across text, image, voice and documents, mapped to MITRE ATLAS, NIST and the EU AI Act); and AI Gateway (routing, securing and governing AI transactions from one control plane, with inline DLP and Zero Trust applied to every model, agent and API call).

quotes: AI Asset Management Auto-discover every AI asset – models, agents, MCP servers, shadow AI – and trace data-to-AI lineage across 2,900+ apps in one unified view.
Secure Access to AI Control who uses AI and how: block access by role in real time, filter sensitive data from LLMs, and govern agent-to-agent traffic.
Secure AI Apps and Infrastructure Test 5,000+ attack scenarios across text, image, voice, and documents, then fix gaps directly – mapped to MITRE ATLAS, NIST, and EU AI Act.
AI Gateway Route, secure, and govern every AI transaction from one central control plane – with inline DLP and Zero Trust applied to every model, agent, and API call in real time.

sub-products.statement: The same page's FAQ says Zscaler AI Security protects the full AI life cycle by combining automated red teaming, dynamic risk assessment and advanced guardrails, and describes AI red teaming as testing and securing AI systems, especially LLMs, by simulating real-world attacks and vulnerabilities such as prompt injection or data poisoning.

quotes: Zscaler AI Security protects the full AI life cycle by combining automated red teaming, dynamic risk assessment, and advanced guardrails.
AI red teaming tests and secures AI systems, especially large language models (LLMs), by simulating real-world attacks and vulnerabilities like prompt injection or data poisoning.

access-security-capabilities.statement: Zscaler's AI Access Security page, titled Secure Access to AI, says it controls access and content across popular GenAI apps, AI SaaS, embedded AI and dev tools, and lists: detecting and classifying thousands of AI apps, including AI embedded in SaaS, with visibility into users, departments, application trends and at-risk data; prompt and response extraction and classification; allowing, blocking or coaching access by user or user group, and policies to warn, block or enforce browser isolation with control over copy-paste; inline DLP on prompts across 100+ DLP dictionaries such as Source Code, PII, PCI and PHI; detecting off-topic or policy-violating use, including toxic, restricted or competitive topics, in prompts and responses; and inline controls for AI IDEs and tools connecting to AI infrastructure.

quotes: Secure Access to AI Control access and content across popular GenAI apps, AI SaaS, embedded AI, and dev tools.
Find a Product, Solution, or Technology >AI Access Security

Detect and classify thousands of AI apps including AI embedded in popular SaaS applications. Get in-depth visibility into users, departments, application trends, and at-risk data with interactive dashboards.
Get a clear view of how users interact with your apps, including deep insights with prompt/response extraction and classification.
Discover which AI apps are being used and by which users. Allow, block, or coach access by users or user groups.
Use flexible policies to warn, block, or enforce browser isolation, giving you full control over copy-paste actions within AI applications.
Block the loss of sensitive data in prompts with powerful inline DLP across 100+ DLP dictionaries like Source Code, PII, PCI, PHI, and more.
Detect off-topic or policy-violating use including toxic, restricted, or competitive topics by analyzing prompts and responses.
Provide developers zero trust access with inline controls for AI IDEs and tools connecting to AI infrastructure, preventing data loss and protecting against cyber threats.

guardrails-page-is-ai-guard.statement: Zscaler's AI Guardrails product address now serves the AI Guard for Users page, which describes AI access decided per user, per app and per risk across 3500+ AI tools with four answers (allow, block, isolate or caution), and names AI Guard for Apps, which inspects prompts and responses in real time inside approved tools, as part of Zscaler AI Security.

quotes: AI Guard for Users Give everyone AI. On your terms.
Access decided per user, per app, per risk, across 3500+ AI tools. Policy reflects who is asking, what they are asking for, and how risky the tool actually is.
Four answers instead of two allow, block, isolate, or caution the user in the moment
Part of Zscaler AI Security Access is the front door. The platform governs everything past it.
AI Guard for Apps prompts and responses inspected in real time inside the tools you approve.

guardrails-page-is-ai-guard.conditions: The capture is the 2026-11-03 recapture of https://www.zscaler.com/products-and-solutions/ai-guardrails, which references/_meta/static-captures.json records as the replacement for the retired AI Guardrails capture; that address now lands on /products-and-solutions/ai-guard-for-users, the capture's source URL. What the earlier capture of the page listed is gap guardrails-page-list.

guardrails-no-separate-surface.statement: AI Guardrails is a product-page name for AI Guard, not a separate configurable product: no Help tree or API carries the AI Guardrails name.
guardrails-no-separate-surface.conditions: Rests on the AI Guardrails page describing AI Guard (guardrails-page-is-ai-guard) and on a search of vendor/zscaler-help and the captured API specifications, which finds no AI Guardrails article tree or API. The AI Security API's guardrail resources are discovered cloud guardrail configurations (AWS Bedrock and Azure), an inventory item, not AI Guard policy.

api-families.statement: The captured AI Security API specification combines two families: AI Infrastructure, 17 operations served from `https://api.zsapi.net/aisecurity/aispm`, and AI Red Teaming, 97 operations served from `https://api.zsapi.net/aisecurity/airt`.

expect.description: API Reference Guide for AI Infrastructure
API Reference Guide for AI Red Teaming

api-families.conditions: Tally over the capture: `jq -c '[.paths[][] | [.servers[].url, .["x-zscaler-source-info"].title]] | group_by(.) | map([.[0], length])' automate-zscaler/openapi/ai-security.openapi.json` returns two groups and no others: 97 operations whose one server is https://api.zsapi.net/aisecurity/airt and whose source is AI Red Teaming, and 17 whose one server is https://api.zsapi.net/aisecurity/aispm and whose source is AI Infrastructure (114 in all); `/info/x-zscaler-source-info` has two entries.

red-teaming-api.statement: AI Red Teaming is the testing side of the family and AI Guard the runtime side: the product page's FAQ describes AI red teaming as testing AI systems by simulating real-world attacks such as prompt injection, and its 97 API operations (AI apps and integration tests, probes, test runs, scheduled tests, reports, remediation) are generated in the aisec surface.
red-teaming-api.conditions: Combines the product page (four-capabilities, sub-products) with the operation list in the captured specification, which `node scripts/kb.mjs surface aisec` prints; no captured Help article documents Red Teaming.

packaging.title: Licensing, SKUs and per-call accounting for AI Guard and the AI Security family
packaging.detail: Unverified legacy statement: AI Guard appears separately licensed, but the SKU and tier mapping is not captured; how inline inspection is billed (per call, per token, flat rate per seat) is not captured. The ZIA integration lists an AI Guard subscription as a prerequisite (ai-security.ai-guard.zia-integration:prerequisites); nothing else states packaging.
packaging.blocks: licensing, entitlement and cost answers for any AI Security product

red-teaming-boundary.title: Red Teaming entitlement, authentication scopes, live acceptance and its link to AI Guard
red-teaming-boundary.detail: Unverified legacy statement: static request and response schemas are captured for the 97 Red Teaming operations, but tenant entitlement, authentication scopes, live endpoint acceptance, and whether Red Teaming remediation or policy-generation output can be applied to AI Guard automatically are unverified.
red-teaming-boundary.blocks: whether Red Teaming can be automated against a tenant and whether its findings configure AI Guard

guardrails-page-list.title: The guardrail list Zscaler's AI Guardrails product page used to carry
guardrails-page-list.detail: Unverified legacy statement: an earlier non-verbatim capture of the AI Guardrails product page (2026-04-24) said it described Zscaler AI Guard as an inline inspection platform for AI applications and infrastructure, with inline guardrails for prompt injection, jailbreak, malicious URL, unreachable URL and invisible text, data protection that leverages 100+ predefined dictionaries and brings AI channels into existing DLP programs, moderation of toxic or competitive outputs, dashboards that show the prompts sent to models, track policy violations and test policies, and support for regulatory frameworks. The current page at that address (AI Guard for Users) states none of it.
guardrails-page-list.blocks: citing a Zscaler product page for AI Guard's guardrail list, including the invisible-text guardrail
